title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is proving Sullivan's de Rham theorem H^q(C_DRS(X,Q)) = H^q(X,Q) for polynomial forms, as motivation for an integral, divided-power version (the subject of his 1976 IHES lecture).

Previous page: E^[n] is the rational affine hyperplane sum x_i = 1 in A^{n+1}. DRS_[n] is its algebraic de Rham complex. As n varies this gives a (semi-)simplicial commutative dga DRS_*. Then C_DRS(X,Q) = Hom(S_*(X), DRS_*).

This page:
(a) C_DRS(X,Q) depends on X only through the singular complex S_*(X).
(b) On semi-simplicial sets, the functor K -> C_DRS(K,Q) is represented by DRS_* in the category of (semi-)simplicial abelian groups.

The proof is a topos-theoretic acyclic-resolution argument in the topos Ss of (semi-)simplicial sets:
(i) DRS_* is a resolution of the constant object Q_*. This is the algebraic Poincaré lemma on the affine spaces E^[n].
(ii) Each degree DRS^i_* is an acyclic object of Ss. Grothendieck says this amounts to pi_j(DRS^i_*) = 0, which is 'easily checked'.
- In modern terms, a simplicial abelian group is Kan, so pi_* = 0 means DRS^i_* -> * is a trivial fibration. That gives the extension property Hom(K, A) -> Hom(L, A) onto for L in K. This is Bousfield-Gugenheim's 'extendable' condition.
- Hence Hom(-, DRS^i_*) computes Ext(Z[K], Q) = H^*(K, Q).
- He remarks that the same works for C^infty, real-analytic or complex-analytic forms on the simplices (Cartan/Whitney-style simplicial forms).

A crossed-out passage: one would like a de Rham-type cochain theory C_DR(X,Z) with integer coefficients, functorial in S_*(X). 'It seems there are obstructions against this! We will get there anyway!'

Then the diagnosis of why the naive Z-version fails. Taking the de Rham complex of E^[n] with its Z-affine structure, the Poincaré lemma fails because integrating x^n dx needs the denominator in x^{n+1}/(n+1).

The cure: divided-power polynomials (formally, power series). If E^[n] came from a free Z-module of finite type, i.e. had an origin, the PD de Rham complex Z<X_1..X_m>[dX] would give a resolution of Z. But the simplex is an affine space, not a linear one.

He records the presentation DRS_[n] = Q[X_i, dX_i]/(sum X_i - 1, sum dX_i), which is isomorphic to Q[X_0..X_{n-1}] tensor the exterior algebra on dX_0..dX_{n-1}.

Next page: the PD analogue fails because 1 - sum X_i is not in the PD ideal. He fixes this by working over a base (S, J, gamma) with t in the PD ideal J, replacing sum X_i = 1 by sum X_i = t.
errors: No real error. 'Acyclic in the topos Ss' iff pi_j = 0 is right in the intended sense (extendability via Kan property of simplicial groups), though stated loosely.
The notation Q[X_0..X_{n-1}][dX_0..] implicitly means polynomial tensor exterior algebra.
Working with semi-simplicial rather than simplicial S_*(X) is harmless for cohomology here.

The crossed-out 'obstructions' claim is vague. Known obstructions (Steenrod operations) concern commutative multiplicative cochain models over Z/F_p, not mere cochain complexes; it is unclear which he meant.

ideas.what: Polynomial de Rham forms on the standard simplices as a simplicial cdga; cochains Hom(S(X), DRS) represent rational cohomology
ideas.modern_name: Sullivan's A_PL / simplicial polynomial forms nabla(n,*)

ideas.what: Proof of the de Rham theorem as an acyclic resolution of the constant sheaf Q in the topos of simplicial sets: Poincaré lemma plus acyclicity of each DRS^i (pi_j = 0)
ideas.modern_name: Extendable simplicial cochain theories / simplicial de Rham theorem (Cartan-style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan (Séminaire 1949-50 on simplicial forms), Sullivan, Bousfield-Gugenheim, Félix-Halperin-Thomas

ideas.what: Integral obstruction: the naive Z de Rham complex of the simplex is not acyclic (x^n dx needs 1/(n+1)); remedy via divided-power polynomials
ideas.modern_name: PD de Rham complex / PD Poincaré lemma; integral models of spaces via PD or binomial algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: PD Poincaré lemma: Berthelot, Cartier (crystalline cohomology). Integral simplicial forms: Cenkl-Porter (1980s); binomial-ring models: Horel, Toën, Kubrak-Shuklin-Zakharov (2020s)

ideas.what: Key obstacle: the simplex is affine without an origin, so the PD structure cannot be transported across sum X_i = 1. This leads (next page) to a PD parameter t with sum X_i = t
ideas.modern_name: PD envelope of a simplex / 'PD simplices' over a PD base

missed.claim: Grothendieck's program for a functorial integral 'de Rham' cochain theory on simplicial sets built from divided-power polynomial forms on simplices, explicitly aware of obstructions, with the declared aim to overcome them. The page identifies the precise failure point: affine structure versus PD structure.
missed.quote: On aimerait avoir une théorie de C_DR(X,Z) ... Mais il paraît qu'il y a des obs. contre! On va pourtant y arriver quand même !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic algebraic models of homotopy types are an active area. Examples: Mandell's E_infinity cochains, Toën's schematization, Horel's binomial rings, derived binomial rings. A PD/simplicial de Rham approach from 1976 anticipates this, and its precise relation to binomial models seems unexamined.

missed.claim: Explicit linking of Sullivan's rational homotopy de Rham theorem with crystalline-style PD de Rham complexes as the route to integral (torsion-retaining) models of homotopy types.
missed.quote: Mais on s'est déjà familiarisé avec une façon de sauter à pieds-joints par dessus ..., en introduisant les p.d. et des polynômes à puiss. div.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bridges crystalline cohomology and integral homotopy theory. Since Z-valued polynomials (binomial rings) and divided powers are closely related, this may be a historical precursor to binomial-ring models of spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is mostly a clean re-proof of Sullivan's theorem (routine). The notable unpublished element is Grothendieck's 1976 plan to get integral homotopy/cohomology models from divided-power polynomial forms on simplices, with the affine-versus-linear obstruction isolated. This is little documented and anticipates later work, though the idea of PD/integral simplicial forms is not wholly absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'S_∞(X)' is almost certainly 'S_*(X)' (the singular semi-simplicial complex).
'(Ss[-≠-](Ens))_*' is likely '(Ss(Ens))_*', semi-simplicial sets, with a struck-out symbol.
'(dans la cat. des groupes ½-gr.[?])' is probably '(dans la cat. des groupes ab. ½-simpl.)', i.e. semi-simplicial abelian groups.
'objets ss acycliques' is probably 'objets acycliques' with an inserted 'ss' (semi-simplicial) or similar.
In the last formula the second factor should be read as the exterior algebra on dX_0,...,dX_{n-1}.
'la cour[?]...' is uncertain; the sense is 'jump over the difficulty'.
